text:
maria: Hey team — FinOps sent a ticket, dedicated cluster 'reservoir-01' seeing repeated 429s for TPS bursts despite showing burst credits >0. Customer complains app sees intermittent timeouts and token-per-second SLOs broken. Can someone take a look? :frowning:

ops-bot: Alert: cluster=reservoir-01 admission_controller.reject_rate spike -> 429s (p95 reject_rate +42% over 5m). Link: https://internal.metrics/redwood/reservoir-01 :rotating_light:

aj: I can grab metrics. Do we have the customer account id and request pattern? Is this many small requests or a few long ones?

maria: Customer pattern: chat-ish traffic, many short generation calls (~50-200 tokens) but bursts from their worker pool — they hit 300 req/s for ~30s. They say they have burst credits recorded in billing panel.

derek: Two quick hypotheses: 1) admission controller token-bucket accounting drift between auth service and admission layer, 2) autoscaler scaled down too aggressively and admission policy enforced conservative headroom during transient scale event.

sam: I just checked autoscaler logs for reservoir-01 around the incident window (1715098700-1715099200). Saw a scale-in triggered at 1715098820 and a resume scale-out at 1715098898. Scaling cooldown was at default 60s which may have been too short for this workload.

sam: pasted metrics snippet:
```
# admission_controller.tokens.available
1715098800 12000
1715098830 800
1715098850 7200
1715098880 600
1715098910 0
# autoscaler.events
1715098820 scale_in reason=low_cpu target=2->1
1715098898 scale_out reason=burst detected target=1->3
```

aj: Weird — tokens.available drops to zero while billing shows credits >0. That suggests an accounting mismatch: billing/costing service vs runtime admission counters. Derek, did we recently deploy the new admission cache invalidation? Could be stale cached account quota mapping.

derek: Yes, we pushed a change last week that caches account->quota mapping in the admission layer for 30s. If the customer's quota was updated (burst credits added) it wouldn't reflect until cache TTL expiry. But the logs should show cache-miss/hit counts. I'll pull admission logs.

derek: Found log lines (trimmed):
```
admission: account=finops-873 cache=HIT ttl_remaining=4s
admission: account=finops-873 cache=HIT ttl_remaining=2s
admission: account=finops-873 cache=STALE -> returning local token state
```

maria: So they got credited but admission layer still using stale token state and refused until TTL expired. That would explain 429s despite billing credits. Two follow-ups: can we accelerate TTL invalidation on quota change events? Also need a mitigation to avoid autoscaler scale-in during credit bursts.

aj: For quick mitigation, ops can temporarily set admission cache TTL to 1s for reservoir-01 and bump autoscaler min_replicas to 2 for 10m. That should give headroom while we fix the cache invalidation path.

sam: I'm applying the quick fixes now: `kubectl patch cm admission-config -n redwood --type merge -p '{\"data\":{\"cache_ttl\":\"1s\"}}'` and `rctl autoscaler set --cluster reservoir-01 --min 2 --until 10m` — will report back.

ops-bot: Deploy event: admission-config patched by sam at 1715099302. autoscaler command executed.

sam: After change, reject_rate dropped to baseline in ~40s. Customers report improved success. But we still need root cause fix: ensure quota update events invalidate admission cache immediately and add a safeguard to prevent scale-in when active burst credits are in flight.

derek: I'll open an engineering issue: 1) subscribe admission service to quota-change webhook to evict cache, 2) add admission-level reconciliation that consults authoritative billing ledger when token-bucket state seems inconsistent. Also propose autoscaler policy change: if recent burst_credit_grant_count > 0, inhibit scale-in for 3m.

maria: Thanks. I'll update the customer: queued a postmortem summary and set expectation for a fix timeline. Also adding a repro in support runbook: curl script that reproduces 429 pattern (send 300 small requests in 30s) and steps to check `admission_controller.tokens.available` and `billing.burst_credits`.

aj: One more note — there was a secondary latency spike (p95 gen latency +1.2s) when autoscaler started new nodes; recommend adding warm pool for dedicated clusters with frequent bursts.

maria: Good catch. We'll add warm-pool recommendation to the playbook. Closing loop: sam/derek, please link the engineering issue here when created and tag me for customer comms.

derek: Issue opened: RD-3981 \"admission cache invalidation + burst credit accounting reconciliation\". Assigned to runtime infra. ETA: 1 sprint. :white_check_mark:

maria: Great, marking as resolved on support side for now. :thumbsup:
